overview: Global and domestic developments unfold today alongside significant local news across various regions. Israel braces for a high-stakes election as rival camps warn of ruin. Anthropic filed for what could be the biggest IPO ever, leading a massive wave of AI dealmaking. Meanwhile, San Francisco's mayor spent millions on signature-gatherers while facing softening poll numbers, and Kauai stories include a flood watch and a shrimp company seeking a state bailout.

items.title: Socialist civil war engulfs Los Angeles mayor race
items.summary: A fight over Israel is fracturing the socialist movement just as it nears a potential victory in the Los Angeles mayor's race.

items.title: Israel braces for an election each side warns could bring ruin
items.summary: Israelis head to the polls today for a consequential election where rival camps warn victory for the other brings ruin.

items.title: Anthropic IPO leads AI's $235 billion dealmaking blitz
items.summary: Anthropic filed for a potentially record-breaking IPO, capping a massive day of artificial intelligence dealmaking that nearly equals one percent of U.S. GDP.

items.title: Oakland, S.F. mayors both want more power. They took opposite roads to get there.
items.summary: Oakland and San Francisco mayors both want more power but took opposite roads, with San Francisco spending millions on signature-gatherers.

items.title: Mayor Lurie’s popularity is high, but has softened, latest polls show
items.summary: New polls show San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's popularity remains high but has softened by about 10 percentage points from its recent high.

items.title: The contrail blues
items.summary: A photo feature captures the contrail blues on 24th Street in San Francisco.

items.title: Flood watch in effect for Hawaii through Wednesday night
items.summary: A flood watch remains in effect for Hawaii through Wednesday night.

items.title: Hawaii justices consider compensation for Schweitzer brothers
items.summary: Hawaii justices are considering whether two brothers wrongly convicted of a 1991 murder can receive compensation for wrongful imprisonment.

items.title: Construction Of Military Data Center On Maui Alarms Residents
items.summary: Residents are alarmed by the construction of a nearly $100 million military data center on Maui that will work with Haleakala telescopes.
